newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets rules on overseas project financing.
newsitem.headline: China sets rules on overseas project financing.

text.p: China issued new rules covering project financing overseas on Friday, saying such projects should have a total investment of $30 million or more and the financing of each project should be $15 million.

Projects without overseas investors should act slowly and carefully when raising funds from abroad because project financing demanded a strong ability to repay the loans and fulfil the contract, said the rules issued by the State Planning Commission and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.
The directive was issued in response to a State Council decree to step up controls over international borrowing.

In recent years, local governments and departments had raised funds on foreign capital markets through project financing to build infrastructure projects, mainly Sino-foreign joint venture power plants, the announcement said.
However, lack of experience and understanding of this type of financing had led to greater difficulties, higher costs of financing and higher prices of imported equipment, it said.
"What's worse, some departments have even guaranteed the payback of loans," the Xinhua news agency quoted an unidentified official as saying.
In addition, some financing had been blocked due to lack of efficient safety measures by the Chinese side with foreign banking institutions hesitant to promise loans, it said.
The new rules demand overseas financing for domestic projects be conducted in a gradual and proper manner.

Project financing should only be allowed for infrastructure projects, especially those that are foreign-funded and need large-scale investment, have a strong capability to pay back the loan and have a long-term, stable income source, the rules say.
The regulations warn that investors and other partners involved in a project have different interests, and under certain conditions these interests may conflict.
Therefore, the main investors of a project should not be partners to carry out the contract, the rules say.

Project financing has resulted in an increase in foreign debt and therefore the proposals and feasibility studies for such projects should be presented to the State Planning Commission for approval. Key projects should be approved by the State Council, or cabinet.
Financing projects should be approved or examined by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange to control costs, ensure cost-effectiveness and the ability to repay the loans, the rules say.

Local authorities should strictly control and guide local project financing activities, especially the costs of financing and construction to ensure the effective use of overseas funds and control over foreign debt, they said.
